name: Невеликий план (1)
description:
It is time to introduce a new strategic theme. Many chess books sometimes give the impression that the best players in the world defeat their opponents by means of a perfectly executed strategic plan, which they have thought out well in advance. In practice, this often turns out to be different. Strategic victories are achieved by an accumulation of small strategic advantages. This is not based on one big master plan, but rather on a series of small plans.

How does such a small plan work? A small plan is the execution of a strategic idea that only covers a few moves. A player tries to gain a small strategic advantage with this.

Below are some examples of small plans:

  • Provoking a weakening in the pawn structure
  • Opening a new front
  • Gaining space
  • Realising a favourable exchange

What do you have to do?

Come up with a small plan to improve your position. Hint: keep the pawn structure in mind.

examples.text: Позиція чорного здається трохи тісною. З 1...f6! чорні можуть раптово вдихнути нове життя в позицію. Зауважте, що 2.f4 не працює добре через 2...fxe5, а білі мають проблеми на лінії f через невигідну позицію білого короля. Хрестоматійний приклад того, як тактика і стратегія поєднуються пліч-о-пліч.

texts: Це відкриває лінії до чорного короля.
Спробуйте відкрити королівський фланг.
puzzles.text: Додаткові переваги полягають у тому, що чорний кінь не має хорошого поля на шахівниці, і чорні також повинні переконатися, що ферзь не потрапить у пастку.

texts: Suddenly, Black's central structure is under pressure.
Pressure the black center.
puzzles.text: White has the bishop pair and wants to open the position. After the c-pawn is exchanged for the black d-pawn, the white bishops have much more mobility.

texts: This creates chances to attack the white king.
Start a kingside attack and make it hard for the white pieces to become active.
puzzles.text: The pawn move is versatile. First, Black tries to open White's king position. This also activates the rook. Note that reducing the tension between the white e-pawn and black f-pawn renders many white pieces inactive. Black can calmly build the attack. For example, by doubling the rooks on the f-file and involving the light-squared bishop in the attack with ...Bc8.

texts: This creates a lot of tension between the pawns and provides attacking chances.
Try to open the position for your pieces.
puzzles.text: White is better developed and wants to open the position quickly. With this break move, White creates a discovered attack on the black rook, and once the center opens, White gains attacking chances against the black king.

texts: White gains space on the kingside and starts an attack.
Launch a kingside attack.
puzzles.text: To make matters worse, White also threatens to win a piece by trapping the Black bishop. Crucially, Black has no counterplay. While White has a clear plan to gain space on the kingside, it's not clear what Black can do.

texts: Black gains space with tempo. Black now threatens to open the long diagonal, creating attacking chances against the white king.
Спробуйте відкрити лінії для своїх фігур.
A prophylactic move. White wants to prevent Black from locking the queenside with ...b5 on the next move.
Make sure Black can't lock the queenside.
puzzles.text: Now that White has prevented the queenside from being locked, the White queen can soon venture out to attack the vulnerable Black pawns.

texts: Це змушує слона визначитися з полем. Після цього білі поля послаблюються.
Спробуйте відкрити лінії для своїх фігур.
puzzles.text: Білопольний слон має зробити незручний вибір. Якщо він відступить, білі здобудуть простір і контроль над центральним полем d5. Якщо ж чорні зіграють слоном на c4, білі можуть розміняти слонів. Після цього розміну контроль над d5 також буде корисним для білих. Крім того, вони зможуть почати атаку по вертикалі f.

texts: White threatens to open lines and disrupt the coordination between the black knights.
Спробуйте відкрити лінії для своїх фігур.
puzzles.text: The main threat now is c4-c5, forcing Black to abandon the defense of the knight on e4. Black is now compelled to make a concession like ...f6-f5, which weakens many dark squares.

texts: This pressures the white center.
Pressure the white center.
puzzles.text: A thematic move in this 'French' structure. The white pawn on d4 comes under fire, and once white captures, the e-pawn is weakened. Additionally, this break move creates more space for the black pieces.

texts: Black gains space on the queenside and seizes the initiative.
Gain space on the kingside.
puzzles.text: White cannot capture because the bishop would be left hanging. This means that Black can gain more space on the next move with ...f5-f4.
